source_caption:
I still can’t believe this was released 58 years ago today. Imagine sitting in a theater in 1968 and watching a computer calmly explain why it won't "allow" you to survive. At a time when most people hadn't even seen a real computer, Stanley Kubrick was already showing us a future where technology develops a mind of its own. 

Beyond the AI, the space scenes and machines were decades ahead of their time. Without a single frame of CGI, Kubrick used massive rotating sets and ground-breaking practical effects to make space feel terrifyingly real. While the rest of the world was focused on the Moon landing, Stanley Kubrick and Arthur C. Clarke were already looking at the "Rise of the Machine." They predicted a world where sentient artificial intelligence could prioritize its own logic over human life decades before the first personal computer even existed. Today, as we actually live in the age of AI, this 1968 "warning" feels less like science fiction and more like a warning that arrived 58 years too early.
